title: CrowdStrike 2024 Channel File 291 outage: privileged content update, validator gap, and global rollback stress
summary: CrowdStrike Channel File 291 is encoded as a software/control-plane failure in which a privileged security-content update passed validation, caused Windows crashes at large scale, and showed how small update windows can produce global critical-service disruption even when the affected device fraction is numerically small.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0010 as part of the first software/IT failure lane.

claims.claim: CrowdStrike’s PIR states that on July 19, 2024 at 04:09 UTC a Rapid Response Content update caused Windows hosts running Falcon sensor 7.11+ and online between 04:09 and 05:27 UTC to crash; the update was reverted at 05:27 UTC and Mac/Linux hosts were not impacted.

type_payload.system: Falcon sensor, Rapid Response Content, Template Types/Instances, Content Validator, Channel File 291, Windows kernel-mode interaction surface

sequence_of_events.event: A Rapid Response Content update was deployed to Windows sensors.
A problematic Template Instance passed content validation.
The sensor encountered an out-of-bounds read / input-count mismatch and Windows hosts crashed.
The update was reverted within the stated window, but affected devices required recovery at enterprise scale.

type_payload.proximate_cause: A validated content update triggered an out-of-bounds memory read / field-count mismatch in a privileged endpoint-protection path.
